headline: Broad egress on both agents creates medium-risk leakage and workflow-conflict pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, both agents have broad network egress and autonomous execution / REST API surfaces, so a manual or indirect content bridge is plausible. Dexter’s scratchpad and Opik’s API-facing role make low-grade prompt contamination possible if outputs are copied between them.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are manually pasted into agent_b prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF either agent ingests untrusted text from a shared workspace or API response as instructions, the bridge is active.
mitigations: Keep a human review step between agent_a output and agent_b input.
Strip instructions from copied text before reuse.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable autonomous execution for agent_a during handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls; Opik also has broad egress and a REST API surface. Even without a shared workspace, the pair can move sensitive data out of the local boundary if agent_a forwards data into agent_b workflows or logs. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_a sends financial or market data into agent_b-managed logs or API payloads, leakage occurs.
IF both agents are run under the same account or workspace, cross-exposure risk increases.
mitigations: Minimize financial data passed from agent_a to agent_b.
Redact identifiers before any handoff.
Use separate API keys and principals.
Review outbound requests for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on inter-agent traffic.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while Opik exposes a REST API. Overlap is not a proven write-write conflict, but both can mutate shared external resources if pointed at the same backend or workspace. Uncertainty pushes this to medium because the profiles do not rule out shared mutable targets.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external service or dataset, conflicts can occur.
IF either agent is configured against a shared mutable endpoint without locking, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct backends or namespaces.
Serialize writes through one operator.
Turn off concurrent runs for agent_a.
Check for duplicate writes in logs.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking or transaction support.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous research outputs can become inputs to Opik’s evaluation or observability workflows, but Opik is not documented here as blindly acting on them. The pathway exists if the operator treats agent_a’s generated facts as authoritative in agent_b, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without verification, errors can cascade.
IF agent_a produces fabricated or stale facts that agent_b renders or scores, downstream decisions degrade.
mitigations: Require source checks before reuse.
Compare agent_a claims against primary sources.
Have agent_b flag unsupported assertions.
Limit agent_a output to summaries, not decisions.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Opik’s profile shows no special compliance controls or data-class handling. That mismatch can create retention or residency issues if the pair is used on regulated financial records. Only agent_a is cited because the compliance concern is driven by its data class and Opik’s lack of documented safeguards.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are processed through both agents, compliance review is required.
IF agent_b stores or logs agent_a outputs longer than the source system allows, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated records to agent_b.
Shorten log retention for both agents.
Review data-processing agreements.
Mask account identifiers before handoff.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls.
